transcript: W: Dev, I read the report from our beverage distributor. Almost every returned case had bottles with hairline cracks.
M: Our inspectors only pull a few bottles from each pallet, so a cracked one can easily slip through.
W: A vendor told me a camera above the conveyor can look at every bottle as it passes and push the bad ones off the line.
M: Every single bottle? At our line speed, I'd need to see that to believe it.
W: They ran our own samples through a test rig last week. It caught every crack but one.
M: Impressive. But the price is steep, and the plant manager is already worried about this year's equipment budget.
W: The returns cost us more in one year than the camera would. I can put the figures in a one-page summary.
M: Good. Send it to me tonight, and I'll read it before I raise the idea with the plant manager tomorrow.
W: I'll e-mail it before I leave. Let me know what she says.

options.A: Why a distributor has stopped ordering from the plant
options.B: How to get inspectors to check bottles more quickly
options.C: A way to catch damaged products before they leave the factory
options.D: Whether to slow the line to protect the bottles

options.A: Give the man a short document covering the costs

options.C: Arrange a second test at the vendor's site

transcript: W: Joel, Mr. Dunmore, thanks for meeting with me. Joel's thesis depends on a set of nineteenth-century harbor maps in the library's special collections.
M1: I need to compare them with modern charts, Professor Lang, but the reading room closes at five, and I teach until four thirty.
M2: I'm afraid those maps are too delicate to photograph or take out of the building. That rule is firm.
W: Could the library scan them instead? Then Joel could study the images wherever he likes.
M2: We do offer scanning, but the waiting list is about three weeks.
M1: That's too long. My first draft is due in two weeks.
M2: Then let me see what I can do, Professor Lang. I could move Joel up the list if you write a short letter of support.
W: I'll write one this afternoon. Joel, once the scans arrive, you can work on them at home.
M1: That would solve everything. Thank you both.

transcript: M: Hello, I have a reservation under Hollis for this Friday, and I need to change the room.
W: Certainly, Mr. Hollis. At the moment you're in our least expensive room, with one queen bed.
M: Right. My wife and our daughter are coming along after all, so we'll need two beds.
W: Two of our rooms have that. One of them also comes with a separate sitting area.
M: We don't need that. Last time we had one, we never used it, and it pushed the price up.
W: Then I'll put you in the other one. It suits families well.
M: Perfect. One more thing: our flight lands at noon. Could we check in before the usual three o'clock?
W: I can't promise that. If housekeeping finishes early, I'll text you. Otherwise, we can keep your bags at the desk until three.
M: That works. Thanks for your help.

transcript: W: Marcus, the author just e-mailed me. She wants a different subtitle on the cover of her cookbook.
M: Now? The cover files are supposed to reach the printer on Thursday.
W: I know. She thinks the current subtitle sounds like it's written for professional chefs, and her readers are home cooks.
M: That's what the sales team requested, though. And the proofs were approved on Monday.
W: Could you make the change and still have the files ready by Thursday?
M: That's a tall order. Changing the words takes me an hour, but the printer charges a fee for any change after the proofs are approved.
W: How big is the fee?
M: Four hundred dollars, plus an extra day on the schedule. I could ask them to waive the fee, but I doubt they would.
W: Don't bother. I'll call the author, explain the cost, and see whether she's willing to keep the current subtitle.

transcript: W: Gus, Theo, thanks for staying after the lunch rush. The seafood supplier called again; half of today's fish never arrived.
M1: That's the second short delivery this month, Elena. And tonight's special is the grilled sea bass.
M2: Should I stop recommending it to tables, Elena? I've already told a few reservations about it.
W: Keep mentioning it, but tell guests it's limited. Gus, how many portions can you cover?
M1: Fourteen. To avoid this in future, I'd move all our seafood orders to Harbor Fresh. They're cheaper, and they've never been late with us.
M2: Hmm. Gus, I'd hate to put all our eggs in one basket. If they have one bad week, we have no fish at all.
W: Theo has a point. Gus, what if we keep both suppliers and split the order, about sixty and forty?
M1: Fine by me. But then I'll need to place the orders two days ahead instead of one.
W: That's manageable. Gus, please send me the new order sheet by Friday, and I'll call both suppliers.

transcript: M: Hi, this is Paul Greer. I have a physical therapy session on Tuesday at nine, but my car goes into the shop that morning.
W: Hello, Mr. Greer. Wednesday is full, but Thursday afternoon has openings. Would two o'clock work?
M: It would. Will my insurance cover it? I've already used five of the six visits my plan allows.
W: Yes, that one is covered. It will be your last, though.
M: My knee still isn't right, so I'd like to book three more visits now.
W: I can't until we get a new referral from your doctor. I can mail you the form, or the doctor's office can fax it directly.
M: Mail would take too long. The doctor's office closes at five, so I'd better hurry.
W: Good idea. Give them our fax number, and your Thursday time will be held for you.
M: I will. Thanks for your help.

transcript: M: Good morning. I own a café on Pine Street, and I'd like to put four tables on the sidewalk this summer.
W: Then you'll need an outdoor seating permit. I can start the application for you right now.
M: Wonderful. How long does it take?
W: About three weeks. First an inspector measures the sidewalk, because five feet must stay clear for people walking by.
M: My sidewalk is pretty narrow, to be honest. Will four tables fit?
W: I can't say until the inspector measures. If fewer fit, you can go ahead with fewer, or withdraw and get your fee back.
M: Fair enough. I'll apply. Do you take cards, or should I go to the bank for cash?
W: Cards are fine at the counter. The form also needs a drawing of the sidewalk showing your door and the tree out front.
M: I have the building plans in my car. I'll bring them in and be right back.
